name: Val Walsh
title: Vice President, Cloud Operations + Innovation
note: Why: CO+I is Microsoft's data-centre organisation — the people who site, build and run the fleet. A DC role at a hyperscaler, not corporate leadership.

name: Jason Taylor
title: Vice President, Infrastructure
note: Why: at Meta he oversaw data-centre expansion and server-chip development; joined Microsoft's data-centre team in a similar role, working under CTO Kevin Scott. A hyperscaler-to-hyperscaler DC move.

name: Sergio Loureiro
title: Vice President, Global Data Centre Operations
note: Why: runs AWS data-centre operations worldwide — strategy, construction and day-to-day management across North America, Europe, APAC and the Middle East. Ranked No. 1 on Data Centre Magazine's Top 100 Data Centre Leaders 2026.

name: Prasad Kalyanaraman
title: Vice President, Infrastructure Services
note: Why: leads AWS Infrastructure Services, the organisation that plans and delivers the physical data-centre estate.

name: Aris Karcanias
title: Head of Data Center Energy & Infrastructure, EMEA
note: Why: appointed June 2026 to lead Google's data-centre energy and infrastructure across EMEA — the power and site side of the hyperscaler build-out in Siddhi's home market.

name: Rachel Peterson
title: Vice President, Data Centers
note: Why: Meta's top data-centre executive, speaking for the Hyperion (Louisiana, scaling to 5 GW) and Prometheus (New Albany, Ohio) campuses.

name: Mahesh Thiagarajan
title: Executive Vice President, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
note: Why: the top of Oracle's OCI organisation, which owns data centres and supply chain alongside compute, networking and storage — the executive the Stargate build-out reports up to.

name: Dan Lawrence
title: Senior Vice President and General Manager, Americas
note: Why: appointed March 2026 to lead Nebius' North American expansion — the gigawatt-scale campus programme in the US — and to scale the organisation behind it.

name: Nazar Khan
title: Chief Technology Officer
note: Why: the executive TeraWulf's data-centre operations report to; co-founder running the technical and site side of the crypto-to-HPC conversion.

name: Sean Farrell
title: Chief Operating Officer
note: Why: promoted to COO from SVP Operations, where he oversaw data-centre operations and the vertical-integration strategy. The release states he continues to report to CTO Nazar Khan — a stated reporting line.

name: Rob Hepler
title: Head of Data Center Operations
note: Why: hired March 2025 to run all operational teams across Core Scientific's HPC data centres, with 500 MW under construction at the time.

name: Michael Stoner
title: Chief Development Officer, North America
note: Why: promoted June 2026 to lead North American development — new campuses and power-ready capacity. The release states he reports to Dana Adams, President North America — a stated reporting line.

name: Alicia Ruckteschler
title: Chief Procurement Officer
note: Why: procurement is the supply-chain bottleneck of every data-centre build (switchgear, generators, transformers); a DC operator's CPO is a DC role. Appointed February 2026.

name: Robin Balen
title: Chief Product Officer
note: Why: leads the newly created product organisation at a data-centre operator — how Vantage packages capacity for cloud and AI customers. Appointed December 2025.

name: John Hatem
title: Chief Executive Officer
prev_title: President — global sales, global procurement, and US design, engineering and construction
note: Why: CEO of a data-centre operator, effective 30 July 2026, promoted from President where he ran sales, procurement and US design, engineering and construction — a delivery-side leader, not a finance appointment.

name: Erich Sanchack
title: Executive Vice President, Operations
note: Why: runs operations for the largest listed data-centre landlord — the operating side of 300+ facilities.

name: Nidhi Chappell
title: Leadership team (ex-Microsoft CVP, Azure AI & HPC Infrastructure)
prev_title: Corporate Vice President, Azure AI and High-Performance Computing Infrastructure
note: Why: at Microsoft she led the design and operation of four generations of the supercomputers behind ChatGPT — the infrastructure side of AI, now at a NeoCloud building its own data centres. Nscale's release does not give her new title, so it is recorded as the leadership team.
